newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq ready to export oil within 48 hours - minister.
newsitem.headline: Iraq ready to export oil within 48 hours - minister.

text.p: Preparations for the flow of Iraqi crude oil to international markets will be ready within 48 hours, Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf was quoted as saying on Thursday.

"During the coming 48 hours and starting from Thursday steps on the ground will be completed for the inspection and gauging of pumping stations," Sahaf said in remarks published in the ruling Baath party newspaper al-Thawra.
"All channels related to the mechanism of implementing the memorandum of understanding are open...and the remaining procedures are quite easy and a few and they do not bear interpretation."
Two experts from the Dutch firm Saybolt arrived in Baghdad on Tuesday to see whether Iraq's oil gauging equipment on the border with Turkey was working properly.
The official newspaper al-Qadissiya said the experts went to Zakho on the Turkish border to "put the final touches" on preparations for the oil exports.

"Iraq succeeded...in making available and in a short period of time all the metering equipment and instruments as well as computers and gauging devices neeeded to make the flow of oil a success," the paper said, quoting Saddam Hassan, chairman of the State Organisation for the Marketing of Oil (SOMO).
The experts were expected in Baghdad on Thursday. They will report to U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros Ghali on their findings later in the week.

The visit by the Saybolt experts is part of preparations for the flow of partial Iraqi exports worth $2 billion in six months under the oil-for-food deal with the U.N. whose terms Baghdad accepted on November 25.

A team from Lloyd's Shipping Intelligence left Baghdad on Tuesday following an inspection tour of Iraq's trade outlets to pave the way for future U.N. inspection of humanitarian supplies reaching Iraq under the oil deal.
